/.description: Docs for humanymous Gate, an open-source Apache-2.0 reverse-proxy engine that scores seven browser signals into an ALLOW / CHALLENGE / DENY verdict. Stops commodity bots; states its T4 ceiling.
/.ogHeadline: Where to start with the docs — humanymous Gate

/start-here/integrator.html.description: Put humanymous Gate, the open-source bot-detection reverse proxy, in front of your app: start in monitor mode, enforce per route once you trust the signal.
/start-here/integrator.html.ogHeadline: Drop Gate in front of your app — humanymous Gate

/start-here/operator.html.description: Operator guide to running the humanymous Gate Ledger: watch ALLOW / CHALLENGE / DENY, triage false-positive spikes vs abuse surges, and use unblock, ban, and the dual-control kill switch. Reference build.
/start-here/operator.html.ogHeadline: Run the Gate from the Ledger

/start-here/evaluator.html.description: Reverse-proxy bot detection you can evaluate: it scores each request across seven layers into an ALLOW / CHALLENGE / DENY verdict. Raises the cost of automation; documents its T4 ceiling. Run monitor mode first.
/start-here/evaluator.html.ogHeadline: Evaluate bot detection for your stack — humanymous

/start-here/developer.html.description: Developer hub to extend the open-source bot detection engine: add signals, scoring, and hard rules, then run the local Red test catalog against your own 127.0.0.1.
/start-here/developer.html.ogHeadline: Extend the engine and its test catalog

/start-here/compliance-dpo.html.description: Gate supports GDPR/PIPA DPO workflows — it does not make you compliant — via pseudonymized identifiers, a tamper-evident audit log, and crypto-shred erasure.

/tutorials/quickstart-monitor-mode.html.description: Stand up humanymous Gate in front of a local app in global monitor mode in 30 minutes: Gate scores and logs every request across layers L1–L7 but enforces nothing.
/tutorials/quickstart-monitor-mode.html.ogHeadline: Run Gate in monitor mode — humanymous

/how-to/deployment-policy-operations.htm.description: How to deploy humanymous Gate — a reference build, not production-hardened: production TLS, origin cloaking (421), RBAC admin tokens, and monitor-to-enforce routes.

/how-to/configure-attested-routes.html.description: Mark a high-value route attested and Gate prices the ALLOW: an unattested ALLOW is demoted to a humanymous Pass, always CHALLENGE→Pass, never DENY. Does not close the T4 ceiling.

/how-to/configure-credential-verifiers.h.description: Configure credential verifiers in humanymous Gate — WebAuthn, Privacy Pass, Web Bot Auth — so proven clients skip the Pass. Off by default; a missing one is a no-op.
keywords: Privacy Pass Private Access Token RFC 9577

/how-to/cut-a-release.html.description: Push a SemVer git tag (vX.Y.Z) and GitHub Actions builds signed core and gate images while git-cliff writes the changelog from Conventional Commits.

/how-to/key-management.html.description: humanymous Gate key management: seal the keystore (SigningSeed, HMACKey, vault) with -keystore + HMN_UNSEAL, size a lost key's blast radius, back it up. Rotation isn't automated in the reference.

/how-to/verify-audit-log.html.description: Verify humanymous Gate's tamper-evident audit log with the public key alone: append-only hash chain, per-record HMAC, Ed25519 Signed Tree Heads, witness co-sign. Detects tampering; records past the last checkpoint stay in-window until sealed.
/how-to/verify-audit-log.html.ogHeadline: Verify the audit log — humanymous Gate

/how-to/observability-siem.html.description: Pull humanymous Gate edge decisions into your SIEM: poll the authenticated admin audit stream with curl and forward. Candid that the reference has no /metrics or health probe.

/how-to/self-validation-red-team.html.description: Red-team a humanymous Gate install you own on loopback: run the bundled bot simulators plus an honest-human baseline, then measure your detection and false-positive rate before you enforce. Defensive-only.

/how-to/detection-observatory.html.description: Run the Detection Observatory, a dev-only, loopback-only page that streams the L1-L7 scoring live so you watch your own engine reach ALLOW / CHALLENGE / DENY.
/how-to/detection-observatory.html.ogHeadline: Watch detection happen, layer by layer

/how-to/audit-console-tour.html.description: Annotated operator tour of the humanymous Gate Ledger console: what each of the six views answers and how to act from it — a reference implementation, not production-hardened.
/how-to/audit-console-tour.html.ogHeadline: Walk the six Ledger views — humanymous Gate

/how-to/upgrade-migration.html.description: Upgrade a self-hosted humanymous Gate node: the reference upgrade is a process restart — keep identity with -keystore, monitor-then-enforce, verify the audit chain across it.
/how-to/upgrade-migration.html.ogHeadline: Upgrade & migrate your Gate node — humanymous

/how-to/troubleshooting-faq.html.description: Symptom-to-fix guide for humanymous Gate integration errors: self-signed cert warnings, HTTP 421 origin bypass, admin API 404, CHALLENGE'd users, and keystore boot. Reference implementation.
/how-to/troubleshooting-faq.html.ogHeadline: Fix Gate integration errors — humanymous Gate

/reference/cli-config-policy.html.description: Complete reference for humanymous Gate: every CLI flag, environment variable, and per-route policy preset (off, monitor, balanced, strict, attested). Reference-build defaults, not production-hardened.

/reference/hard-rules-verdicts.html.description: Lookup tables mapping each verdict — ALLOW, CHALLENGE or DENY — to its edge action, the hard rule that fired it, and drill-down signal IDs. Apache-2.0 build.
/reference/hard-rules-verdicts.html.ogHeadline: Reading a verdict row — humanymous Gate

/reference/supported-topologies.html.description: Which of the seven detection layers fire per topology: JA3/JA4 TLS fingerprinting runs only when the process terminates raw TLS; behind a CDN it goes inert.
keywords: Gate reverse proxy vs Core engine
L4 TCP passthrough PROXY protocol v2
/reference/supported-topologies.html.ogHeadline: Where each detection layer is active — humanymous

/reference/install-requirements.html.description: humanymous Gate install requirements: Go 1.25.3, one direct dependency (uTLS), pure Go with no CGO, cross-compiles to Linux, macOS, Windows. Reference build needs no database or Redis.
/reference/install-requirements.html.ogHeadline: What you need to install humanymous Gate

/reference/red-team-catalog.html.description: Reference map of humanymous's 47 Red-team bot profiles: 45 must-block bots, one honest T4 detection ceiling, one human baseline, plus seven raw-protocol attacks. Local-only.

/reference/production-vs-reference.html.description: humanymous Gate is an Apache-2.0 reference build, not production-hardened. Each dev-grade stub — ephemeral keys, self-signed TLS — is named with its prod-delta.
/reference/production-vs-reference.html.ogHeadline: Reference build vs production — humanymous Gate

/reference/deployment-cost-latency.html.description: Deployment cost of humanymous Gate: it adds four inline per-request work terms and no published benchmark — a sizing framework to measure in monitor mode.
/reference/deployment-cost-latency.html.ogHeadline: Sizing Gate cost and latency — humanymous Gate

/reference/rbac-separation-of-duties.htm.description: humanymous Gate admin-plane RBAC and separation of duties: four roles (Auditor, Operator, Approver, DPO), capability-resolution rules, and dual-control that bars self-commit.
/reference/rbac-separation-of-duties.htm.ogHeadline: Who can do what on the admin plane — humanymous Gate

/reference/standards-mapping.html.description: Maps humanymous Gate's reference-build controls to GDPR and PIPA articles and the RFCs they use, plus a repeatable DSAR audit evidence-pack. Controls support your obligations; they do not discharge them.

/reference/data-processing-inventory.htm.description: Field-by-field GDPR Article 30 (RoPA) inventory of the personal data humanymous Gate observes versus stores: raw signals scored in memory, only scrypt-derived 64-hex pseudonyms at rest. Supports your record; does not certify compliance.
/reference/data-processing-inventory.htm.ogHeadline: Build your Article 30 RoPA — humanymous Gate

/reference/security-audit.html.description: Pre-release Red/Blue security audit of the humanymous bot detection engine: GO-with-fixes; every confirmed finding remediated, residual T4 detection floor disclosed.

/reference/security-disclosure.html.description: Coordinated-disclosure policy template for a humanymous Gate deployment: how researchers report a vulnerability, what is in scope, and the good-faith safe harbor.

/reference/support-licensing.html.description: humanymous Gate ships under Apache-2.0 as a reference implementation, not a production-hardened build; its Go dependencies are BSD-3-Clause and MIT, and support is deployment- and vendor-specific.

/reference/versioning-derivation-index.h.description: Maintainer reference: how humanymous Gate docs are versioned — scoring-policy version vs signed config_version — and how each page derives from an internal spec.
/reference/versioning-derivation-index.h.ogHeadline: How the docs are versioned and derived — humanymous

/explanation/what-gate-is.html.description: humanymous Gate is a reverse-proxy engine that scores seven browser signals into an ALLOW / CHALLENGE / DENY verdict. Reference build; names its T4 ceiling.
/explanation/what-gate-is.html.ogHeadline: What Gate is, and is not — humanymous Gate

/explanation/where-gate-fits.html.description: humanymous Gate decides human vs automation at the edge, complementary to your WAF, CDN, and CAPTCHA. Reliable on commodity bots; names its T4 ceiling.
/explanation/where-gate-fits.html.ogHeadline: Where Gate fits vs WAF, CDN, CAPTCHA

/explanation/which-piece-am-i-using.html.description: One scoring engine, three surfaces: the standalone detection engine on :8443, the enforcing Gate reverse proxy on :8444/:8445, and the read-only Detection Observatory. Names which one you are touching.
keywords: standalone detection engine vs Gate proxy
/explanation/which-piece-am-i-using.html.ogHeadline: Which piece am I using? — humanymous

/explanation/will-this-break-my-app.html.description: Gate can score and log without enforcing (monitor mode), fails open on safe GET reads, and reverts instantly; an uncertain verdict becomes a PoW challenge, never a silent block.
/explanation/will-this-break-my-app.html.ogHeadline: Will bot detection break my app? — humanymous Gate

/concepts/how-gate-sees-a-request.html.description: How humanymous Gate sees a request: it scores seven browser and TLS layers into one ALLOW / CHALLENGE / DENY verdict at the edge, and names its T4 ceiling.
keywords: how bot detection sees a request
/concepts/how-gate-sees-a-request.html.ogHeadline: How a request moves through humanymous Gate

/explanation/detection-engine-internals..description: How the humanymous detection engine scores signals into one ALLOW / CHALLENGE / DENY verdict: per-signal severity, noisy-OR combine, a 60% per-layer cap, and 21 first-match hard rules.
/explanation/detection-engine-internals..ogHeadline: How the engine reaches a verdict — humanymous

/explanation/control-plane-and-bundle.ht.description: Gate's /__hmn/ control plane and injected bundle: reserved edge endpoints (loader.js, session, collect, csp-report) plus one add-only HTML loader tag.
/explanation/control-plane-and-bundle.ht.ogHeadline: The /__hmn/ control plane & bundle — humanymous Gate

/explanation/observatory-architecture.ht.description: humanymous's Detection Observatory is a dev-gated, local-only page that renders the engine's own ScoreTrace — the same code that scores each request, not a copy that can drift.

/explanation/red-catalog-architecture.ht.description: How humanymous builds its Red catalog: 47 local-only attack fixtures plus a Go uTLS client that test your own detector against a human baseline and the honest T4 ceiling.
/explanation/red-catalog-architecture.ht.ogHeadline: How the Red catalog is built — humanymous

/explanation/transparency-report.html.description: Transparency report for humanymous bot detection: what data it collects, how ALLOW/CHALLENGE/DENY is decided, its GDPR basis, and the T4 ceiling it names.

/explanation/how-this-was-built.html.description: Spec-first, adversarially self-validated: this bot detection method traces every scored signal from written intent to verified verdict, and names its T4 ceiling rather than hiding it.
/explanation/how-this-was-built.html.ogHeadline: How this bot detection engine was built — humanymous

/runbooks/incident-runbooks.html.description: Symptom-indexed on-call runbooks for a humanymous Gate deployment: triage and respond to DENY-spike false positives, scraping, HTTP/2 floods, AI-agent waves and audit-integrity alerts, with dual-control rollbacks.

/runbooks/kill-switch-and-bans.html.description: Operator runbook for humanymous Gate's kill switch and bans. The kill switch demotes hard-rule enforcement fleet-wide to monitor; manual bans keep enforcing.
/runbooks/kill-switch-and-bans.html.ogHeadline: Kill switch & bans runbook — humanymous Gate

/runbooks/erasure-crypto-shred.html.description: Crypto-shred destroys the per-subject linkage key binding audit-log pseudonyms — DPO-gated, dual-control, with a cancellable hold window. Records stay verifiable.

/reference/on-call-quick-reference.html.description: On-call cheat sheet for humanymous Gate: verdict legend, top hard rules, ban levers, kill switch, and 20-second attack-vs-false-positive triage. Reference build.
/reference/on-call-quick-reference.html.ogHeadline: Run an on-call shift on Gate — humanymous

/help/why-am-i-seeing-this.html.ogHeadline: Why am I seeing this? — humanymous Gate
